rulings.Case Title: JON THOMAS FREEMAN VS. TIBERIAN DESIGN, A CALIFORNIA CORPORATION IN PROIC
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, August 4, 2026, Line 1, PETITIONER JON FREEMAN's Notice Of Court Hearing. Off calendar without prejudice to being re-noticed. There is no proof of service on Mr. Morelli of either the petition or the notice of court hearing. (See In re FairWageLaw (2009) 176 Cal. App. 4th 279 (principal shareholders who may have claims against each other are entitled to notice and opportunity to litigate those claims before the corporation is wound up)). For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/HEK)

rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, August 4, 2026, Line 8, 1- DEFENDANTS EQUITY RESIDENTIAL MANAGEMENT, L.L.C. and EQR-855 BRANNAN LP (DE)'s Demurrer to First Amended Complaint. Defendants Equity Residential Management, L.L.C. and EQR-855 Brannan LP's demurrer to the third cause of action for battery, the fourth cause of action for false imprisonment and the eighth cause of action for fraudulent concealment in the first amended complaint is sustained with leave to amend by August 25, 2026 to the third and fourth causes of action and sustained without leave to amend as to the eighth cause of action. The first amended complaint does not allege any ultimate facts showing that the alleged battery and false imprisonment by defendant Larry Pryor was committed in the course and scope of any employment or agency by Equity or EQR. rulings.Case Title: LIZ JENDRYSIK VS. KAISER FOUNDATION HEALTH PLAN, INC. ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, August 4, 2026, Line 9, DEFENDANTS JACQUELINE BROOKS , MFT, KAISER FOUNDATION HEALTH PLAN, INC., AND THE PERMANENTE MEDICAL GROUP, INC.'S MOTION TO STRIKE FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT. Defendants' motion to strike the punitive damages allegations in the first amended complaint filed by plaintiff Isabel Jendrysik is granted as to all the punitive damages allegations without prejudice to seek leave to amend to allege punitive damages allegations if and when Jendrysik is able in good faith to allege sufficient facts to support punitive damages on some or all of her claims against some or all of the defendants.Wholly apart from the applicability of inapplicability of CCP 425.13 to any of defendants or any of Jendrysik's claims, none of the claims alleged in the first amended complaint sufficiently allege either malice, fraud or oppression, the predicates for punitive damages, or authorization, ratification, or participation in the malicious, fraudulent, or oppressive conduct by an officer, director or managing agent of the entity defendants.
